content: Sodium fluoride is a dental agent that has been approved by the FDA for the prevention of dental caries. A common adverse reaction associated with its use is dental fluorosis. For adults, sodium fluoride is indicated to aid in the prevention of dental cavities. The recommended dosage involves using the product once daily after brushing your teeth with toothpaste. To administer, hold the bottle upright, squeeze it, and fill to the designated fill line. This will dispense the correct dose of 10 milliliters. Vigorously swish the 10 milliliters of rinse between your teeth for one minute, then spit it out. Off-label use of sodium fluoride in adults is not well-documented, and there is limited information regarding guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported off-label uses. One potential off-label indication is for sensitive dentin. For pediatric patients aged six years and older, sodium fluoride is also indicated for the prevention of dental cavities. The dosing instructions are the same as for adults: use once daily after brushing with toothpaste, dispense 10 milliliters, swish for one minute, and spit out. For children under six years of age, consultation with a dentist or doctor is recommended. There is limited information regarding off-label use in pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or not. There is limited information available regarding contraindications for sodium fluoride in the drug label. Warnings include keeping the product out of reach of children. If more than the amount used for rinsing is accidentally swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Adverse reactions are not well-documented in clinical trials or postmarketing experience for sodium fluoride. Drug interactions with sodium fluoride are not well-documented in the drug label. There is no FDA guidance on the use of sodium fluoride in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, specific gender or racial populations, patients with renal or hepatic impairment, women of reproductive potential, males, or immunocompromised patients. Sodium fluoride is administered orally. There is limited information regarding monitoring, IV compatibility, and overdose. In the event of suspected overdose or poisoning, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately. The mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of sodium fluoride are not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information regarding clinical studies, how the product is supplied, and storage instructions. There is limited information regarding patient counseling for sodium fluoride. The interaction between alcohol and sodium fluoride has not been established, so patients should consult their doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication. One brand name for sodium fluoride is ACT Anticavity Fluoride Cinnamon. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for sodium fluoride.
